items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I went up and told the Prestige – Bob Weinstock about him, and he sent for him.

ctx.x: Take us through some of those days at Prestige.

That was – his thing was – it was like a factory, a music factory. He didn’t approach recording the music the way they did at Blue Note. At Blue Note they were much more considerate. They were much more concerned with hearing what you’re going to play before you actually record it. Bob Weinstock didn’t really care about that. He just wanted to have the cats there go in the studio and hit. He knew we were going to play some music. So he didn’t have to hear it first, because he sort of assumed that it was going to…
What kind of bread were you making?
